Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the detailed demo last week. As we start mapping internal roadmaps, the leadership team asked for a concrete proposal that ties GPU reservation sizing to our expected deal milestones. Attached is our latest demand profile (hourly TPS estimates by model and environment) — should help ground sizing.

Top asks from our side:
- A set of 2–3 reservation options (cluster size, minimum GPUs, and an example ramp schedule).
- Suggested fallback strategies if we undershoot/overshoot (e.g., automatic burst to hosted, model Qs for cheaper variants).
- Example SLA language around sustained throughput and planned ramp windows.

We’d like the proposal to feed into procurement this month; happy to take a short call to walk through options.

Best,
Rajiv
VP Engineering | PraxisBio

Rajiv — thanks for the profile, that’s perfect. Looping Ben and Karthik from our deals team so they can propose concrete reservation options and the commercial framing.

Quick notes from an initial pass:
- We can structure three clear lanes (Conservative / Expected / Aggressive) with explicit min-GPU floors and ramp phases.
- Ramp phases typically use a 4–12 week activation window depending on integration complexity (we’ll propose both a fast and a measured path).
- For cost control, we recommend a mixed-quantization profile and a prefix caching policy for the QPS pattern you shared.

Ben / Karthik — can you draft the three lanes and include an example cost delta and SLA implications? Rajiv, I’ll make sure we call out the mutual action plan for procurement timelines.

Rajiv / Marissa — attaching a concise set of options below (summary here, I’ll upload a one-page comparison into the deal record):

Option A — Conservative (Low-risk entry)
- Cluster: 16x A100 equivalent GPUs
- Min guaranteed: 4 GPUs (warm pool + hot lane)
- Ramp: 4 weeks to 16 GPUs (2-week pilot at min guaranteed)
- Use case: early integration + pilot traffic
- SLA: 99.5% uptime on reserved capacity; burst to hosted up to 30% of sustained load

Option B — Baseline (Expected growth)
- Cluster: 48x A100 equivalent GPUs
- Min guaranteed: 16 GPUs
- Ramp: 8–10 weeks, staged (16 -> 32 @ week 4 -> 48 @ week 8)
- Use case: production launch + steady growth
- SLA: 99.9% uptime on reserved capacity; predefined burst windows with cost-sharing model

Option C — Aggressive (Fast scale)
- Cluster: 96x A100 equivalent GPUs (or mixed A100 + H100 lane)
- Min guaranteed: 32 GPUs
- Ramp: 12 weeks with 2x warm start credits for first 4 weeks
- Use case: rapid expansion, high-availability model serving
- SLA: 99.95% uptime, dedicated standby capacity, quarterly SLA review

Tradeoffs and considerations:
- Cost: A -> B = ~2.9x cost uplift; B -> C = ~1.7x uplift (back-of-envelope, depends on model mix / quantization).
- Model variants: Recommend deploying a 7B quantized variant for lower latency paths and keeping a 13B/34B full-precision variant behind on the same cluster (auto-fallback by policy).
- Warmup / caching: Plan a 2-week synthetic warmup for KV cache + prefix cache size tuning before traffic cutover. This reduces cold-call latency and token cost spikes.

Attachments: Draft_SLA_redlines.pdf (internal redlines; will send a customer-facing clean copy after we align).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm which lane aligns to the board / procurement appetite (Rajiv).
2) We’ll produce a mutual action plan with dates and acceptance criteria (Marissa + Ben).
3) Legal review of SLA redlines (we can pre-wire a 30d response window).

Happy to hop on a 30-min call today if you have availability.

— Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — concise alignment from my side. Rajiv, two small clarifications then a proposed MAP (mutual action plan):

Clarifications:
- Do you expect a single region primary (us-east-1) for launch or an immediate multi-region requirement? That changes min GPU and warm-standby sizing.
- Any hard dates from procurement for contract signature? We’ll align the ramp milestones to those dates.

Proposed MAP (high level):
- Week 0: Sign SOW + initial 30% commitment (reserve min guaranteed)
- Week 1–2: Integration sprint + synthetic warmup; run sampling traffic to validate KV/prefix caching
- Week 3–6: Stage 1 ramp to mid-lane (e.g., 16 -> 32 GPUs) with weekly telemetry checkpoints
- Week 7–12: Full ramp to committed slate, enable cost controls and fallback policies

Action items:
- Rajiv: confirm region and procurement target date (reply inline)
- Marissa: I’ll draft the MAP in HubSpot and attach a short SOW template with the three lanes and SLA language
- Ben: finalize customer-facing proposal and cost delta table; propose two signature-ready options (B + C) for procurement to evaluate

Link to draft MAP in deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567
Calendar: https://calendar.redwood.ai/meeting/ben-30m (30m)

Onward — I’ll prepare the SOW by EOD Monday once Rajiv confirms region/date.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions | Redwood Inference
